data.label: Flux Dev
data.description: Black Forest Labs Flux Dev. Text-to-image with guidance, seed, and negative prompt control.

negative.label: Negative Prompt
negative.description: What to exclude from the image.

guidance.label: Guidance Scale
guidance.description: How strictly to follow the prompt. Higher = more literal.

seed.label: Seed
seed.description: Leave empty for random. Set for consistency across shots.

lora.label: LoRA Reference
lora.description: Path or ID of a LoRA model for style or character consistency.

data.claude_guidance:
Flux Dev responds best to detailed, descriptive prompts. Lead with subject and composition — what is in the frame and how it is framed. Follow with lighting specifics (source, quality, direction). Mood and cinematic style go last.

Be specific about textures, materials, and colors. Avoid vague emotional language; translate feelings into visual descriptions (e.g. instead of 'melancholy', write 'desaturated blues, long shadows, empty space in frame').

Negative prompts are effective. Always include quality control terms: blurry, low quality, watermark, text, artifacts. Add anything the shot must not contain.

Guidance scale 7–9 works for most shots. Push to 12–15 for highly controlled, specific looks. Stay below 7 for more creative interpretation.

Set seed when visual consistency across shots in a scene matters. Leave empty for variation.

Do not describe camera movement in the text field — that belongs in v_setup tokens. Keep prompts under 200 words.

data.label: WAN 2.1
data.description: Wanx 2.1 video generation model. Strong motion quality and prompt adherence for cinematic shots.

text.label: Prompt
text.description: The video generation prompt describing motion and action.

negative.label: Negative Prompt
negative.description: What to exclude from the video.

reference_image.label: Start Frame
reference_image.description: Image to use as the first frame of the video.

data.claude_guidance:
WAN 2.1 is a video model — prompts must describe motion, not static scenes. Lead with camera movement (dolly in, crane shot, static hold, slow pan). Follow with what the subject is doing. End with environment and atmosphere.

Describe the arc of the shot from first frame to last. If the shot is static, say so explicitly — 'camera holds, no movement' — otherwise the model may add unwanted drift.

Negative prompts are supported. Include: blur, jitter, stuttering, low quality, artifacts.

For duration: 4s is standard for a shot. Use 6–8s for slow, atmospheric shots or complex action.

Reference image (start frame): strongly recommended. Use the image BONE output for the same shot as the start frame for visual continuity.

Keep prompts under 150 words. WAN 2.1 responds better to direct, concrete descriptions than to stylistic language. Say what the camera sees happening, not how it feels.

data.label: Seedance 2
data.description: ByteDance Seedance 2. High-fidelity video generation with strong motion coherence and cinematic quality.

reference_image.label: Start Frame
reference_image.description: Image to use as the first frame.

data.claude_guidance:
Seedance 2 excels at cinematic, high-motion content. Prompts should read like a camera operator's shot card — precise and physical.

Lead with camera movement and lens behavior (e.g. 'slow dolly forward', 'handheld follow', 'static wide'). Then describe the primary subject action in concrete physical terms. Environment and lighting details close the prompt.

Seedance 2 handles complex motion well — do not shy away from multi-element action. It also respects cinematographic language, so v_setup tokens (cu, dolly, noir) translate well into prompt phrasing.

Negative prompts are NOT supported by Seedance 2 — omit the negative field entirely.

Duration: 5s is the standard shot unit. Use 10s only for establishing shots or sustained action sequences.

Provide a start frame reference image whenever possible — Seedance 2's image-to-video quality is significantly stronger than text-only generation.

Keep prompts focused and under 120 words. Seedance 2 degrades with over-specified prompts.

data.label: Kling v2
data.description: Kuaishou Kling v2. Text-to-video and image-to-video with camera control, mode selection, and strong motion quality.

mode.label: Mode
mode.description: Pro mode for higher quality at additional cost.

reference_image.label: Reference Image
reference_image.description: Image to use as the first frame.

camera_control.label: Camera Movement
camera_control.description: Explicit camera control parameter — overrides text-described movement.

data.claude_guidance:
Kling v2 has a dedicated camera_control parameter — use it instead of describing camera movement in the text field. Set camera_control to the appropriate value from the options list, then do NOT describe that same movement in the text prompt (it causes conflicts).

In the text prompt, focus on: subject appearance and action, environment, lighting, and visual style. The camera is handled by camera_control.

Negative prompts are supported and effective. Include quality terms: blur, distortion, artifacts, low quality.

Mode: use 'standard' for most shots. Use 'pro' for hero shots, establishing shots, or anything that will be prominent in the final cut.

Duration: 5s is the standard unit. 10s for slow establishes or extended action.

Kling v2 responds very well to reference images. Use the image BONE output as the start frame whenever available — the resulting video will be significantly more consistent with the intended frame.

Keep text prompts under 150 words. Avoid camera language in the text field since camera_control handles it.

data.label: Flux Schnell
data.description: Black Forest Labs Flux Schnell. Fast, low-cost image generation for drafts, previews, and iteration.
data.claude_guidance:
Flux Schnell is the fast, low-cost sibling of Flux Dev — use it for drafts, storyboard previews, and iteration before committing to Flux Dev for finals.

Prompt style is the same as Flux Dev: lead with subject and composition, then lighting, then style. However, Schnell is less sensitive to prompt detail — simpler prompts work fine for drafts.

Negative prompts are NOT supported by Flux Schnell — omit the negative field.

Guidance scale is fixed internally — no parameter to set.

Because Schnell is a draft tool, seed consistency matters more here than in Flux Dev. Set seeds when iterating on a specific shot so you can compare prompt variations against the same base.

Keep prompts under 100 words. Schnell degrades less gracefully with long prompts than Flux Dev does.
